question.problem:
$$
f(x)∼{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }{b}_{n}\operatorname{sin}⁡(nx)
$$

Let $F(x)=3$ for $x\in [0,\pi ).$ The Fourier sine series of the **odd** $2\pi $-periodic extension $f(x)$ of $F(x)$ is shown above. Find the expression for ${b}_{n}.$

$\,{b}_{n}=$ {{field-1}}
question.worked_solution:
For our Fourier sine series, the coefficients are given by

$$
{b}_{n}=\frac{2}{\pi }{\int }_{0}^{\pi }f(x)\operatorname{sin}⁡(nx)\,\text{d}x.
$$

In our case, $f(x)=3$ for $x\in (0,\pi ).$ So, substituting into the formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{b}_{n} & =\frac{2}{\pi }{\int }_{0}^{\pi }3\operatorname{sin}⁡(nx)\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{6}{\pi }{\int }_{0}^{\pi }\operatorname{sin}⁡(nx)\,\text{d}x \\  & =-\frac{6}{n\pi }[\operatorname{cos}⁡(nx)]_{0}^{\pi } \\  & =-\frac{6}{n\pi }(\operatorname{cos}⁡(n\pi )-\operatorname{cos}⁡(0)) \\  & =\frac{6(1-\operatorname{cos}⁡(n\pi ))}{n\pi }.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, since $\operatorname{cos}⁡(n\pi )=(-1)^{n},$ we have

$$
{b}_{n}=\frac{6(1-(-1)^{n})}{\pi n}.
$$
